## Purpose

`dataprep.qmd`'s current *Street Intersections* section calls `ox$graph_from_polygon()` once per study-area unit (~200 units, processed in waves) against the live Overpass API — the same shared, rate-limited, sometimes-overloaded endpoint that has already caused repeated trouble in this project (timeouts, mirror-switching). This document operationalizes an offline alternative: clip and filter the Illinois OSM extract locally with `osmium`, build the drive-network graph **once** for the whole county with `ox$graph_from_xml()`, and run the exact same `project_graph()` → `consolidate_intersections()` logic `dataprep.qmd` already has, unchanged. No Overpass request, no per-unit run list, no resume logic — one call instead of ~200.

This is a planning/validation document, not a live pipeline change: it lays out and verifies the approach in detail so it can be adopted into `dataprep.qmd`'s *Street Intersections* section once validated (see *Relationship to `dataprep.qmd`*, below).

## Why This Works — Verified, Not Assumed

`graph_from_xml()` parses a static local OSM XML file into the same kind of graph `graph_from_polygon()` builds from a live Overpass response, so the downstream code (`project_graph()`, `consolidate_intersections()`, coordinate extraction) is reusable unchanged. But two things about it needed checking before relying on it, so this was verified directly against the installed `osmnx` package (2.1.1) source and a live `osmium` (1.16.0) install, rather than assumed:

- **`graph_from_xml()` takes no `custom_filter`/`network_type` argument, and applies no tag-based filtering at all.** Its signature is `graph_from_xml(filepath, *, bidirectional=False, simplify=True, retain_all=False, encoding="utf-8")` — nothing like `custom_filter`. Tracing its parse path (`_osm_xml._overpass_json_from_xml()` → the SAX `_OSMContentHandler` → `graph._parse_nodes_paths()` → `graph._create_graph()`) confirms every `<way>` element in the file becomes a graph edge, unconditionally — there is no highway-tag check anywhere in that chain. This means the `highway_subtypes`/`service_exclusion`/`access`/`aeroway`/`indoor` filtering `dataprep.qmd`'s `drive_filter` currently applies *via the Overpass query string* must instead happen **upstream, in the file itself**, before `graph_from_xml()` ever reads it — that's what Step 2 below does with `osmium tags-filter`.
- **`.pbf` is not accepted.** `graph_from_xml()` hard-parses the file as XML (`etree_parse`/SAX). Feeding it a binary `.pbf` file would fail outright. The `.pbf` → `.osm` XML conversion in Step 2 is required, not optional — this settles the "worth a quick test rather than assuming" question from the original three-step sketch.
- **Orphaned nodes from the filtering passes are handled automatically, not left over as junk.** Removing ways in Step 2 doesn't remove the nodes those ways referenced — but `graph_from_xml()`'s default `retain_all=False` (matching every existing per-unit call in `dataprep.qmd`) discards every graph component except the largest one, which drops those now-isolated single-node leftovers with no extra cleanup step needed.

## Step 1 — Clip Illinois to Cook County (`osmium extract`)

Reuse the Illinois `.osm.pbf` `dataprep.qmd` already downloads via `osmextract::oe_read()` for the *Streets and Speed Limits* section (`https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/illinois-latest.osm.pbf`) — no second download needed.

`osmium extract --polygon` requires a GeoJSON **Feature** (verified live: a bare `Polygon` geometry is rejected with `Expected 'type' value to be 'Feature'`) in geographic (lon/lat) coordinates. `sf::st_write()`'s GeoJSON driver produces a `Feature`/`FeatureCollection` by default, so exporting the already-built `cc_boundary` (from `dataprep.qmd`'s *Study Area Geography* section) just needs the right CRS:

```r
library(sf)
cc_boundary_geo <- st_read("data/boundaries/cc_boundary.shp") |> st_transform(4326)
st_write(cc_boundary_geo, "data/boundaries/cc_boundary.geojson", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

`osmium-tool` is a system package (C++), not an R or Python package — but since it's available on conda-forge, it can be installed into the existing `osmnx-env` conda environment and run from R through `reticulate`, without ever leaving RStudio for a separate terminal:

```r
reticulate::conda_install("osmnx-env", packages = "osmium-tool", channel = "conda-forge")

# confirm it's actually reachable in that environment before relying on it
reticulate::conda_run2(cmd = "osmium", args = "--version", envname = "osmnx-env")
```

With that done, `reticulate::conda_run2()` runs any `osmium` subcommand inside `osmnx-env` the same way — `cmd` is the executable, `args` is a plain character vector of the command-line arguments (**not** `cmd_args` — that argument name doesn't exist and raises `unused argument`), and `envname` picks the conda environment:

```r
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "extract", "--polygon", "data/boundaries/cc_boundary.geojson",
    "illinois-latest.osm.pbf",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_extract.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

file.exists("data/osm/cook_extract.osm.pbf")
```

One caveat worth knowing before chaining several of these calls (Step 2 does exactly that): `conda_run2()` joins `args` with a plain space, without quoting each element individually. That's harmless for every argument used in this document (none contain spaces), but an argument that did contain one would need its own quoting added manually.

## Step 2 — Filter to the Drive Network (`osmium tags-filter`)

`osmium tags-filter` matches a `w/key=value1,value2,...` expression syntax (verified live: comma-separated values within one expression are matched as alternatives), and `-i`/`--invert-match` flips a pass from "keep matches" to "drop matches." Chaining a keep-pass with several invert-match exclude-passes reproduces `drive_filter`'s exact logic:

```
'["highway"~"{highway_subtypes}"]'
'["service"!~"{service_exclusion}"]'
'["access"!~"private"]["aeroway"!~".*"]["indoor"!~"yes"]'
```

as five sequential `osmium tags-filter` passes (verified live end-to-end on a synthetic file: a `service=driveway` way present after the keep-pass was correctly dropped by the following invert-match pass, while an unrelated way was left untouched):

Each pass is a separate `reticulate::conda_run2()` call, feeding the previous pass's output into the next:

```r
# 1. Keep only the drive-network highway subtypes (same list as dataprep.qmd's highway_subtypes)
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "data/osm/cook_extract.osm.pbf",
    "w/highway=primary,primary_link,unclassified,residential,secondary,secondary_link,service,tertiary,tertiary_link,trunk,trunk_link,busway,construction,corridor",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_01_highway.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 2. Drop the service-road exclusions (parking aisles, driveways)
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_01_highway.osm.pbf",
    "w/service=parking_aisle,driveway",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_02_service.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 3. Drop private-access ways
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_02_service.osm.pbf",
    "w/access=private",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_03_access.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 4. Drop anything tagged as an aeroway (any value)
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_03_access.osm.pbf",
    "w/aeroway",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_04_aeroway.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 5. Drop indoor=yes, and output straight to OSM XML (osmium's -f/--output-format
#    works on any command, so this folds the pbf-to-XML conversion into the last
#    filtering pass rather than needing a separate `osmium cat` step)
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_04_aeroway.osm.pbf",
    "w/indoor=yes",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_drive_network.osm", "-f", "osm", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

file.exists("data/osm/cook_drive_network.osm")
```

The intermediate `.osm.pbf` files (passes 1–4) keep the pipeline fast; only the final output needs to be XML, since that's the only file `graph_from_xml()` reads.

## Step 3 — Build the Graph Once, Reuse Existing Logic Unchanged

```r
G_drive <- ox$graph_from_xml("data/osm/cook_drive_network.osm", retain_all = FALSE)
G_drive <- ox$project_graph(G_drive)

intersections <- ox$consolidate_intersections(G_drive, rebuild_graph = FALSE, dead_ends = FALSE)

coords_df <- intersections$to_crs("EPSG:4326")$get_coordinates()
lon <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(coords_df$x$to_numpy()))
lat <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(coords_df$y$to_numpy()))

cook_intersections <- tibble::tibble(lon = lon, lat = lat)
```

`retain_all = FALSE` and the `consolidate_intersections()` call are identical to `dataprep.qmd`'s `get_area_intersections()`; the coordinate-extraction pattern (numpy array, not a converted pandas object) is the same one already used there for the same reticulate-conversion-safety reason. This single call replaces the entire run-list/wave/`pwalk()`/Overpass-mirror machinery in `dataprep.qmd`'s current *Street Intersections* section.

## Practical Notes

- **Study-area attribution is lost and must be restored.** Each per-unit Overpass call in the current approach got its `geoid`/`name`/`type` attribution "for free," since the call itself was scoped to one unit's polygon. A single countywide `graph_from_xml()` call has no such scoping — the result is one flat table of intersection points with no unit attribution. Restore it with an explicit spatial join against `study_area` after Step 3: `st_join(st_as_sf(cook_intersections, coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326), study_area)`.
- **No resume/checkpoint logic is needed**, unlike the current run-list/wave system — that machinery exists specifically to survive mid-run Overpass failures, a failure mode this approach doesn't have (there's no live query to fail). Re-running for an updated OSM snapshot is just re-running Steps 1–3 against a freshly downloaded Illinois `.osm.pbf`.
- **This changes only how the input graph is sourced, not the consolidation algorithm** — `consolidate_intersections()`'s tolerance, `rebuild_graph`, and `dead_ends` arguments are unchanged from `dataprep.qmd`.
- **Validate before trusting it as a full replacement.** Before retiring the Overpass-based approach, compare this method's output on a handful of already-processed municipalities against the corresponding per-unit results already on disk — a materially different intersection count for the same unit would indicate the filter chain in Step 2 doesn't fully match `drive_filter`'s intent and needs a closer look.

## Task Table

| Task | Description | Output | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clip Illinois to Cook County | `osmium extract --polygon` against `cc_boundary`, reusing the Illinois PBF `dataprep.qmd` already downloads | `cook_extract.osm.pbf` | Not started |
| Filter to the drive network | Five-pass `osmium tags-filter` chain (one keep-pass, four invert-match exclude-passes), final pass outputs OSM XML directly | `cook_drive_network.osm` | Not started |
| Build the countywide graph | `ox$graph_from_xml()` once, then the existing `project_graph()`/`consolidate_intersections()` calls, unchanged | Countywide intersection point table (replaces the per-unit run) | Not started |
| Restore study-area attribution | Spatial join of the consolidated intersections against `study_area` | `all_intersections_sf` with `geoid`/`name`/`type` attribution | Not started |
| Validate against existing output | Spot-check intersection counts for a sample of municipalities against the current per-unit results | Validation comparison | Not started |
| Retire the Overpass-based run list | Once validated, replace `dataprep.qmd`'s wave/resume machinery in *Street Intersections* with this approach | Simplified `dataprep.qmd` (future edit, out of scope for this document) | Not started |

## Relationship to `dataprep.qmd`

This document plans and verifies the approach; it does not itself change `dataprep.qmd`. Once validated per the task table above, `dataprep.qmd`'s *Street Intersections* section would be rewritten to use Steps 1–3 here in place of its current run-list/wave/Overpass loop — the rest of that section's downstream consumers (the combine step, `output/all_intersections.shp`, the `phase01.qmd` interactive map) are unaffected, since they only depend on the final `all_intersections_sf` schema (`geoid`, `name`, `type`, `geometry`), not on how it was produced.
